evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'I just need to ask you more questions about the move might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time?' — framing is present (time-boxed) but rushes past without waiting for explicit yes before continuing to 'Do you have any important concerns...'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'Do you have any important concerns about this move that you also want to discuss on the call?' — asked before any logistics probing, customer replied 'Not, not right now.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised no concerns, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Customer raised no concerns, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (house to apartment), floor/stories (one story house, first floor apartment), rooms/size (2800 to 800 sq ft one bedroom), walking distance (5-8 miles / close proximity), special considerations (downsizing, leaving furniture behind), parking (driveway to alley), additional items (detailed inventory: TV, couch, bed frame, clothes on rolling racks, kitchen table, exercise bike, nightstands, lamps, boxes ~10-15), addresses (2101 Willowbrook Way to 690 Executive Drive, Centric 190 complex).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Joanna: 'Do you need help packing stuff into boxes?' Customer declined for now.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'Do you think we'll have around thirty or forty boxes in total...?' Customer: 'Just about ten' then revised to 'maybe Max fifteen if that.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically for a inventory list of size which is pretty much like a one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours to complete... estimated budget of $580 but if it goes up to three and a half hours that would be $782, including the transportation fee already.' Range given ($580–$782), personalized to customer's inventory (small list, already moving some items himself).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna disclosed: $102/hour per mover ($204 for two), two-and-a-half-hour minimum, charges in 15-minute intervals after minimum, $75 transportation fee one-time, everything else included (blanket pads, shrink wraps, disassembly/reassembly, taxes, insurance, credit card fees).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Joanna never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. After giving the range, she moved directly to 'would you like our help for this move on the twenty sixth?' with no pause for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'on time guarantee if we run late on the time that we schedule we provide discounts for your move.' — discount term disclosed in recognizable form.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'no worries, damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.' — $2,000 coverage stated; framing that it's built into the rate is implied ('no hidden fees of any type'), but does not explicitly state 'no deductible / no fine print.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Joanna never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closing question. The call moved directly to the ask after the Two Promises section with no loop-close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Joanna never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent. No final genuine concerns check before the ask.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Joanna never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'would you like our help for this move on the twenty sixth?' — plainly asked, but customer immediately provided an out: 'Let me, I got some other quotes coming in but you all sound right there in the ballpark...' Joanna then softened the path further: 'I'll go ahead and send everything to you in an email so you have something to read on as well and if you're ready to go ahead with the booking you can just respond to the email or give us a call whichever works for you.' No hard ask executed.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Never mentioned; no rate-lock or deposit discussion.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial: Joanna confirmed date (26th), phone (email address taken: steven[AT]gmail.com), but arrival window not explicitly confirmed, crew size not specified, and no review of addresses or notes left for crew concerns. Call ended with 'I'll send everything to you in an email' without a definitive booking or next-step confirmation call.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (inventory list, both addresses, parking, floor layout, downsizing situation) and delivered a personalized, anchored price range ($580–$782) that directly reflected the customer's small item count and simplified move profile.
coaching_note: After pricing, always ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold silence for customer reaction before moving to the ask; this call jumped straight to the ask without that critical validation, and then abandoned the ask entirely when the customer mentioned competing quotes rather than asking directly to earn the business.
